pr_body:
This PR brings Bundles Widget - Grouped containers of files/folders for quick access from the home page. **Example usage** - Group your useful programs or games with a little help from bundles. - Access your workload files quickly without browsing a single folder!
**Features of this PR** - MVVM Ready - `IDisposable` Ready - Flexible `BaseJsonSettingsViewModel` for serialization! - `DynamicDialog` for dynamic dialogs - any dialog could be created off of it! (MVVM Ready) - Overhauled `Interaction.OpenSelectedItems` -> `Interaction.OpenPath` - Minor Improvements - Bundles UI **Things yet to do** - [x] Improve UI - [x] Setting for disabling/enabling Bundles - [x] Add "Add Bundle" UI - [x] Remove, Rename Bundles - [x] Remove items from Bundles - [x] Folder Icons - [x] Icons don't show bruh - [x] Right click option to open folders in new tab - [x] View does not update when performing actions with bundles - [x] Drag and Drop does not cover entire Bundle area - [x] Show big add button when there are no Bundles - [x] Big Add Bundle button is not being hidden - [x] Replace `Interaction.OpenSelectedItems()` with `Interaction.OpenPath()` [Help wanted] - [x] Add Translation strings [Help wanted] - [x] Add option to export bundles configuration file - [x] Add option to import bundles - [x] Fix columns plz @yaichenbaum - [x] Remove the reveal border from bundles [Help wanted] - [x] Remove the reveal border for items in bundles [Help wanted] - [x] Fix code style 🤯 **Screenshots (constantly updated)** ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53011783/104122194-cbada080-5343-11eb-86f4-d506332fd3b2.png) ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53011783/104122200-d6683580-5343-11eb-91b0-faec55065a89.png) **Future Bundles PR #3637** - Option to rearrange Bundle items by dragging - Select items upon `OpenPath` navigation - Ability to rearrange Bundles - TBD: Support for adding shourtcut files - Display warning when creating a Bundle if the name already exists #3449
Closes #1465

issue_context.title: Containers for Pinned Items on the Home Page
issue_context.body:
This request is corresponding to the widget system announced in #366  

**Idea:**
My suggestion is to introduce a widget that allows users to create storage containers on the home page, which can be filled with links to folders, files and programs. This will enable them to access everything related to one topic from one location instantly, regardless of where the files are stored on the system, like the current explorer sidebar. But instead of having an unorganized and overloaded sidebar, this gives users flexibility and order. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61259627/87483931-f8863280-c602-11ea-995f-552121a679b7.jpg)

@XPoppyX also suggested to allow different sorting any layout options for these containers, as he already included in this screenshot. Personally, I'm not sure about the layout modes, as the limited space doesn't really allow for different displays that would still stay clear, but this can of course be explored in the future.

**Dependencies:**
Currently Files UWP doesn't support drag and drop from one folder to another as far as I know, which makes filling these containers a bit more complicated. as a drag 'n' drop alternative and especially if this is nothing that will be possible in the future, I would suggest to offer a context menu entry. I know that the context menu is kind of sensible in the way that it gets confusing quickly with additional elements, but I don't really see any other viable solution. The only other thing I could think of is an own selection window, that could be opened from the target container.But this would be less user friendly imo.

So this is my try on using tiles: I tried two sizes. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58466626/87775660-c0f7d000-c826-11ea-9457-62f9c5323a14.png)

While the medium large tiles alleviate the issue of too little space for the label, I don't think anybody would benefit from larger Icons or Previews, as you usually only put things in there you use often and therefore already know the content of. But as mentioned, you have very little space for the file/folder/program name in the small tiles version.

I've also thought about scaling and I want to hear what you all think. For hand-scaling the containers, I would provide a hard grid based on the width and height of the fields. You can't increase the width by half a field, it will snap to the whole width immediately (like in the win10 startmenu). 
For window-scaling I'm not quite sure and it also depends on the implementation of the whole widget system. Generally, I would define a minimum and maximum width for a field and if it gets too short, either put the whole container into a second row below or move it beyond the window's right edge and make it side-scrollable. I would prefer to have a second row because you have everything visible at every moment. But I wouldn't have any issues with scrolling downwards or sidewards internally inside a container.
